if the mass is strictly posterior to the aorta, the esophagus is often spared from direct compression.", "Distinguish this configuration from anterior or encasing masses: a posterior location relative to the aorta makes dysphagia less likely than cough (due to airway irritation or vagal involvement), whereas anterior displacement of the aorta would suggest different pathology and symptomatology."]}, {"category": "localization", "trigger": "When evaluating bilateral air space opacities on a chest X-ray to determine the underlying etiology based on distribution and symmetry.", "steps": ["Assess the symmetry of the opacities by comparing the left and right lung fields;
